cards.design_implication: If designing an instrument with polarization-sensitive bolometers that requires high-precision absolute calibration, consider implementing a mapmaking solution like SRoll that utilizes orbital dipoles and foreground templates to correct for detector nonlinearities and bandpass differences.
does_not_establish: That this calibration method is applicable to non-bolometric detectors or other frequency ranges.
That this method eliminates all systematic errors, only that it minimizes residuals.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The SRoll mapmaking solution for the 100–353 GHz channels minimizes map residuals between all HFI detectors at a given frequency, using absolute calibrations based on the orbital dipole, together with a bandpass-mismatch model constructed from spatial templates of the foregrounds and a parametric model characterizing the remaining systematics.
limitations: Applies specifically to the Planck HFI instrument and its 2018 data release processing.
Depends on the availability of accurate spatial templates for foregrounds.
cards.statement: The SRoll mapmaking algorithm for Planck-HFI channels uses absolute calibrations based on the orbital dipole, combined with bandpass-mismatch models and systematics characterization, to minimize map residuals and achieve high precision.

cards.design_implication: When modeling data from instruments measuring polarization via bolometer differencing, acknowledge that polarization angle and efficiency errors are degenerate and can induce mode leakage; design controls or calibration routines must address these coupled systematic effects.
does_not_establish: A method to definitively separate these two parameters if only in-flight data is available without prior constraints.
That these leakage effects are negligible; the text implies they are significant enough to require correction.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The SRoll mapmaking algorithm assumes the ground-based measurements of polarization angles and eficiencies, which cannot be separated because they are degenerate with each other. Errors in the polarization angles induce leakage from E to B modes, while errors in the polarization eficiencies lead to gain mismatch between I, Q and U.
limitations: Specific to the Planck HFI PSB (Polarization-Sensitive Bolometer) architecture.
Reflects the state of knowledge and algorithm assumptions during the 2018 data release analysis.
cards.statement: In the Planck analysis, the effective polarization efficiencies and polarization angles of the HFI bolometers are treated as degenerate parameters, where errors in these values induce leakage between E and B modes and gain mismatches.

cards.design_implication: For analyses combining low-multipole polarization with high-multipole spectra, establish a conservative boundary where TE low-multipole data may be excluded if simulations show excess variance, relying instead on EE data within the ℓ < 30 range for optical depth constraints.
does_not_establish: The physical cause of the excess variance in the TE spectrum at low multipoles.
That TE data is unusable for all low-multipole analyses, only that it was excluded here for robustness.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The T E spectra show excess variance compared to simulations at low multipoles, most notably at = 5 and at $\ell = 1 8$ and 19, for reasons that are not understood. No attempt has been made to fold in Commander component-separation errors in the statistical analysis. We have therefore excluded the T E spectrum at low multipoles (with the added benefit of simplifying the construction of the SimAll likelihood).
limitations: Specific to the SimAll likelihood construction for the 2018 Planck release.
The exclusion is due to unexplained variance, not necessarily a universal physical constraint on TE.
cards.statement: The low-multipole polarization likelihood (SimAll) used for cosmological parameter constraints in this study is restricted to the multipole range ℓ = 2 to ℓ = 29 and relies solely on the EE spectrum, excluding TE due to unexplained excess variance.
